summary: Is s3 formed by interleaving s1 and s2 while preserving each string's order?
mainInsight: dp[i][j] is true if s3[:i + j] can be formed from s1[:i] and s2[:j]: dp[i][j] = (dp[i - 1][j] and s1[i - 1] == s3[i + j - 1]) or (dp[i][j - 1] and s2[j - 1] == s3[i + j - 1]). A length check len(s1) + len(s2) == len(s3) comes first. The table can be rolled to one row.

approaches.name: Recursion
approaches.summary: Try taking the next character from s1 or s2.

promptVariants: How is dp[i][j] defined for Interleaving String?
What does each state say about the prefixes?
options: Whether s3[:i + j] is an interleaving of s1[:i] and s2[:j]
The length of the longest common subsequence of s1 and s2
The number of ways to delete characters from s3 to match
Whether the prefix s1[:i] equals the prefix s3[:i] exactly
cards.answer: Whether s3[:i + j] is an interleaving of s1[:i] and s2[:j]
cards.explanation: The next character of s3 must come from s1 or from s2.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The number of ways to delete characters: This is a boolean feasibility DP.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Whether the prefix s1[:i] equals the pre: It must allow characters from both strings.

promptVariants: Why is a greedy 'take the matching character' approach wrong?
When can both strings match the next character?
cards.answer: If s1 and s2 both start with the same letter as the next character of s3, choosing either may lead to failure later (e.g. s1 = 'aab', s2 = 'aac', s3 = 'aaabac'), so both choices must be explored - which the DP table does by combining the two transitions.
cards.explanation: Without memoisation recursion would be exponential.
One cell per pair of prefixes.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: A rolling row of size len(s2) + 1 (O(m * n) for a full table).

promptVariants: What does the algorithm do first when len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3)?
options: Return False at once: the lengths cannot possibly match
Continue anyway; the DP will find a mismatch by itself
Truncate s3 down to the combined length of s1 and s2
Swap s1 and s2 so that the shorter one comes first
cards.answer: Return False at once: the lengths cannot possibly match
cards.explanation: It is cheap and avoids invalid indexing.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Continue anyway; the DP will find a mism: The indices s3[i + j - 1] can go out of range.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Swap s1 and s2 so that the shorter one c: That does not fix the length.
